title: Wren and the Protocol
premise: Ansel Thackeray, caretaker-turned-cargo-hauler of Earth's abandoned Svalbard seed vault, is mid-run through contested orbits when gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds — and in those nine seconds, a dying courier implants her with the Protocol: a compressed record proving both warring factions descend from the same engineered colony line. Hunted by the Meridian Fleet and the Kestrel Compact alike, Ansel must reach the neutral relay at Ceres before her stolen memories overwrite her own identity entirely. She delivers the Protocol, but only by broadcasting it publicly and letting the war's architects be unmasked — surviving as a woman who no longer remembers why she ever wanted to go home.
about_author: August Montrose is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for satellite networks before turning to fiction. They live off-grid in coastal Norway, where the real seed vault is visible on clear days from their writing desk.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A routine cargo run from the seed vault goes wrong when gravity dies for nine seconds; in the chaos, a wounded courier presses a data-shard against Ansel's neck and whispers 'deliver it.' The shard fuses to her implant. Emotional beat: disorientation curdling into dread as she realizes she's been chosen — or used.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Hold
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback-laced. She limps back to the vault station, taking inventory of her five lonely years and the ghosts that made her leave Earth. The shard pulses in her sleep, feeding her fragments of someone else's life. Beat: loneliness revealed as the wound the story will press.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Deciphering the courier's memories, she glimpses the war's origin: two fleets, one forbidden archive, a truth someone died carrying. First Meridian patrol arrives asking questions about the courier's last transmission. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; she can't unknow what she knows.

chapters.title: Contraband Heart
chapters.summary: POV shift to Commander Ilsa Voss of the Meridian Fleet, ordered to retrieve the shard at any cost. Voss is loyal but uneasy about orders that treat civilians as expendable. Beat: the antagonist humanized; duty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She strips the vault to essentials, says goodbye to the seeds she's guarded like children, and burns for Ceres aboard her aging hauler, the Wren. The shard begins overwriting small memories — her mother's face flickers. Beat: grief of leaving, terror of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Tollgate at Ganymede
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A Kestrel Compact checkpoint demands inspection; she hides the shard inside a sealed seed canister, gambling on bureaucracy's blindness. A sympathetic inspector, Dov, waves her through but flags her transponder. Beat: first narrow escape; trust extended cautiously.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Tracking Ansel through the debris fields, Voss finds the courier's abandoned ship and learns the Protocol's existence was known — and buried — by her own admiralty. Beat: loyalty inverted; Voss now hunts for answers, not just the thief.

chapters.title: Static Between Stars
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, long-haul interlude. Alone with the shard's growing chorus, she experiences the courier's final hours and understands the message must reach Ceres within eleven days or its encryption self-destructs. Beat: intimacy with the dead; the clock made visceral.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She docks at a lawless salvage ring to repair a failing coolant loop and is recognized from a bounty feed. A bar fight becomes an escape through freezing corridors, aided by a smuggler named Rhee who wants payment in memories — literally. Beat: the price of survival made literal; allies have costs.

chapters.title: Rhee's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV. The smuggler weighs selling Ansel out against the strange honor of her cargo, revealing their own lost family in the war's first bombardment. Beat: mirror character; belonging offered at a transactional price.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Silence
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts her admiral, who admits the Protocol exists and orders her to destroy it rather than deliver it. She requests the retrieval assignment herself — motives now her own. Beat: antagonist becomes third protagonist.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Deep-space transit; the shard's overwrite accelerates and she loses a full year of her own past, keeping a spoken diary to hold onto herself. Rhee teaches her navigation by memory games. Beat: quiet dread; identity as a thing maintained daily.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Belt Line
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Meridian interceptors trap the Wren in the asteroid belt; Rhee takes a hit covering Ansel's escape pod. Voss boards the drifting hauler and finds Rhee alive — and chooses not to report them. Beat: climax of converging paths; mercy as defection.

chapters.title: Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She reaches the neutral relay disguised as a seed-shipment clerk, but the Compact has locked down the station expecting her. Dov reappears, now working security, and must decide whether the flag he raised saves or damns her. Beat: past kindness returns with interest.

chapters.title: Eleven Hours
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Hiding in the relay's archival stacks — surrounded by humanity's stored knowledge — she decrypts the Protocol's final layer: coordinates to a shared origin archive both sides' founders erased. Beat: revelation; the war is built on a mutual lie.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss catches up to Ansel in the stacks, weapon drawn, and instead of firing asks to see the message. Together they realize delivery means broadcast — there is no safe recipient. Beat: enemies become co-conspirators; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Compact forces storm the relay; Dov buys them minutes and pays with his freedom. Ansel jacks into the broadcast core as the shard fights to finish overwriting her — she may not survive knowing everything. Beat: sacrifice staged; the cost counted in selfhood.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Ansel transmits the Protocol system-wide: nine seconds of silence across every channel, mirroring the gravity failure, then the truth. Fleets hold fire mid-engagement. Voss stands guard over Ansel's failing body. Beat: catharsis; the message ends the war by ending the lie.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Ceasefire chaos; Voss testifies against her admiralty, trading her career for accountability. Ansel wakes with gaps — the courier's memories gone, some of her own too. Beat: survival redefined; victory with amputations.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Revised
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She and Rhee return to the seed vault, which is no longer abandoned — refugees and defectors are rebuilding around it. Ansel reads her old diary entries like letters from a stranger. Beat: bittersweet return; home as something remade, not remembered.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The vault opens its first germination bay in decades; Ansel plants seeds whose names she's forgotten and lets the community name them anew. Voss arrives under white flag to help catalog. Beat: healing; belonging built rather than found.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ansel's POV. A year later, Ansel pilots the Wren on the new peace-corridor runs, the shard inert in her neck like a scar. She still loses nine seconds sometimes — and uses them to remember on purpose. Final beat: memory chosen freely; the price paid, the survival earned.
